root_cause: In Table._render, box_segments was built as [head, foot, mid] tuples of (left, right, vertical) segments, but rows select from it with `box_segments[0 if first else (2 if last else 1)]`. Index 1 (every middle row) therefore got the foot_* characters and index 2 (the last row / footer) got the mid_* characters, so mid and foot box elements were swapped.
best_solution: In rich/table.py::Table._render, reorder the box_segments list to [head, mid, foot] (move the foot_left/foot_right/foot_vertical tuple after the mid_* tuple) so it matches the index expression `0 if first else (2 if last else 1)`. Reasoning from the statement: 'mid appeared in the footer, footer appeared mid body' means two positions are swapped; grep table.py for `foot_left`/`mid_left`, find the list of segment tuples, then read the consumer indexing to see index 1 = middle, 2 = last.
hidden_test_demands: New tests/test_table.py::test_placement_table_box_elements parametrized over (show_header, show_footer) in {F,T}x{F,T}: box=box.ASCII with every box attribute overwritten via table.box.__dict__.update to unique letters/digits, padding=0, 4 fixed-width columns, 2 rows + add_section + 1 row, Console(record=True, width=28).export_text() compared exactly. Requires body rows to use mid 4/5/6 and the final row (footer if shown, else last body row) to use foot 7/8/9; section divider uses row_* and footer divider uses foot_row_*.
locating_signals: Title/body name 'box elements', 'mid', 'footer', and the attribute names head_left/mid_left/foot_left etc. Grepping `foot_left` in rich/table.py lands directly on the box_segments list in Table._render (function not named, but only one site).
our_outcome_summary: All four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8) PASS in the Kaggle env with a patch byte-identical to gold (swap the foot and mid tuples). v7 additionally left a stray repo-root test_box_order.py scratch file (harmless to grading). Pod runs: v6 36s/15 calls, v4 76s/21, v7 84s/25, v8 96s/40.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement says two visual/positional roles are swapped (X shows where Y should, and vice versa), find where the ordered collection is built AND where it is indexed, and fix the order in the collection to match the index expression rather than patching the consumer. Delete scratch repro/test files you created before finishing so the final diff contains only the fix.
acceptable_alternatives: Changing the index expression to `box_segments[0 if first else (1 if last else 2)]` instead of reordering the list is behaviorally equivalent and should pass the same test.
